$comment: Operator rulings the v2 report schema waits on. Seeded mechanically from the Report Schema Rulings page export (questions: entries.json; decisions: answers/report_decisions/*.json; chat decisions after the export: a flagged overlay); `status` flips to "decided" only by transferring the operator decision, never by hand-editing a row source. RS-5 FAILs every row still pending on a decided ruling.

decision_vocabulary.drop: decided: the recommendation is replaced by the note

rulings.gap: On 93,123 half-semi lots, the detached house, house + suite and houseplex cards assume the attached half is removed. Today one of those can become the headline, and RD semis carry no disclosure saying so.
rulings.recommendation: Recommendation: add a flag requires_attached_half_removed. Flagged rows never become the headline; they show as cards with a badge, and a new disclosure attached_half_removal applies in every zone including RD.

decision.note: Operator in chat 2026-10-20: "Can semi's be identified? If yes, then just the renovations card should show. This will allow for the use to input the key data and then generate teh costs." → On a half-semi lot show ONLY the renovation cards (no new-build cards, so no headline from a detached form). Supersedes the flag/badge recommendation.

rulings.gap: The estimate uses the whole semi footprint for one half, so renovation figures and basement/addition costs are about 2× too high on ~53,000 halves.
rulings.recommendation: Recommendation: use half the shared footprint as the estimate on a half-semi lot, disclosed as an estimate, until the owner enters their own.

decision.note: Operator in chat 2026-10-20: "maybe we dont even show our renovation data on the semi's and just require user input to solve that problem. as per the issue that it maynot be a semi - include a way for the user to tell us if it isnt so we can show the whole picture if it s a detached instead." → On a half-semi lot: no estimated existing-house figures at all; the renovation cards require the owner's input before showing numbers. Add a user correction 'this is not a semi (it's detached)' that switches the lot to the full report (all new-build cards). Supersedes the halve-the-footprint recommendation.

rulings.gap: A secondary suite in a semi is deferred (M-214(3)), but suite add-ons can appear on the semi houseplex and semi renovation cards.
rulings.recommendation: Recommendation: no suite add-on on semi houseplex or semi renovation cards; show the deferred disclosure instead.

decision.note: Operator in chat 2026-10-20 (semi lots show only renovation cards) — no suite add-on on semi cards follows from that.

rulings.key: Rear-suite CoA vs your earlier ruling LC-49
rulings.gap: You approved a CoA version of the rear suite today. LC-49 (Spec 131) says CoA does not apply to the rear suite.
rulings.recommendation: Recommendation: amend LC-49 to allow it, but show it as not evaluated (coa_factor_unfitted) until there are enough realized CoA suites to calibrate it.

decision.note: Operator in chat 2026-10-20: "does the COA grant variances to these suites if so then we should keep it". Measured (local dev DB, read-only): 1,129 CoA applications mention a garden suite (607) or laneway suite (522) since 2018-11-21; 865 approved, 132 refused. So keep the rear-suite CoA: amend LC-49, shown as not evaluated until calibrated.

rulings.key: Same-form comparables vs your earlier ruling LC-51
rulings.gap: You approved comparables by build type. LC-51 says no new field for comparables.
rulings.recommendation: Recommendation: no new stored field. Filter the existing comparable_builds list by build type when the report is assembled, so LC-51 still holds.

rulings.gap: Addition (back/up) already uses the renovation envelope. Expanding the envelope needs its own definition to be a separate card.
rulings.recommendation: Recommendation: Addition = a targeted addition up or back sized by the owner; Expanding the envelope = keep the house and build out to the full renovation envelope (renovation_envelope_gfa_sqm − existing). Reject with a note if you meant something else.

rulings.key: Open the app contract (Spec 100) for report identity and media
rulings.gap: Spec 100 excludes zoning and geometry today. The report needs zone label, lot frontage/depth, the map outline, the Street View block and the offers list.
rulings.recommendation: Recommendation: amend Spec 100 to whitelist these, server and mobile in one commit, with offers as a separate top-level list (never inside lot data).

decision.note: Operator "y to Q7" (2026-10-20): Spec 100 will be amended to whitelist identity (zone label, frontage/depth, map outline), street_view and offers. Offers are first-party targeted ads in a separate top-level list, always labelled Sponsored. Rows move to the consumer/presentation source, marked pending:spec100_amendment until the Spec 100 amendment (app lane) lands.

page_export.note: This will be targeted ads from us

rulings.gap: Spec 126 defines placements; Spec 128 makes the Sponsored label mandatory. No placement policy is set.
rulings.recommendation: Recommendation: two slots: after the scenario cards (detail_footer, already declared) and in the renovation section (renovation contractors). Never inside a card. Always labelled Sponsored.

rulings.key: Street View photo for the renovation section
rulings.gap: Web builds a Street View URL on the client with a public key; mobile has none. Google terms allow caching the panorama id but not the image; cost is per image.
rulings.recommendation: Recommendation: fetch on the server (find the panorama, aim it at the lot, sign the URL), cache only the panorama id, always show attribution, cap usage with a kill switch, never use the photo as data. Re-check Google current pricing and terms first.

Recommendation: v1 uses about 33 static illustrations keyed by scenario × roof form × suite type × semi, captioned Illustrative — not this lot. A per-lot massing drawing from the card numbers comes later.

decision.note: Each scenario shown will have a few different photos with it..

rulings.gap: Today cost is per lot, not per scenario; no spec owns per-scenario cost.
rulings.recommendation: Recommendation: the Spec 88 cost lane owns it: each scenario card prices its own floor area with the existing rates, after the scenario step exists.
